is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles arabiensis, a major malaria vector in Ethiopia (Abstract, page 2).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports on Vgsc-L995F (page 2, 8), Ace-1 G280S (page 8), and Rdl-A296S (page 8).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper provides allele frequencies for various markers across multiple sites and seasons (Figure 2, Figure 3, Figure 4, and Table 1 for sample sizes).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from fifteen field sites across Ethiopia (Methods, page 3; Table 1, page 5).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original empirical study using whole-genome sequencing of field-collected samples.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides specific sampling sites (e.g., Agnuak, Asossa, Arbaminch, Dilla, etc.) and coordinates (Table 1, page 5).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study reports collection years 2020-2023 (Table 1, page 5).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study uses new collections from 2020-2023 as part of the Malaria Vector Genome Observatory.

supplement.evidence: The provided PDF includes all necessary tables and figures, including the supplementary tables (Table S1-S4) and figures.

assessment.summary: This study performed whole-genome sequencing on 1272 Anopheles arabiensis mosquitoes collected from 15 sites across Ethiopia between 2020 and 2023. It analyzed the spatial and temporal distribution of known insecticide resistance markers (Vgsc-L995F, Ace-1 G280S, Rdl-A296S) and metabolic resistance-associated CNVs (Cyp6aa/p, Cyp9k1, Gste2, Coeae2-7g, Cyp6z2). The study found significant geographic and seasonal variation in these markers and identified novel selection signals using genome-wide scans.
